questions.prompt: Which command turns a new directory into a Go module?
questions.explanation: `go mod init <module-path>` creates the `go.mod` file that makes the directory a module, recording its path, Go version, and dependencies.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between `go run` and `go build`?

options.text: `go run` compiles and runs without keeping a binary; `go build` produces a reusable executable
`go run` only checks types; `go build` runs the program

questions.explanation: `go run` is for quick iteration (no binary left behind); `go build` compiles a binary you can ship or run again.

questions.prompt: The file that records verified cryptographic checksums of dependencies is ____.
questions.explanation: `go.sum` records checksums so future downloads are verified to match what you originally built against; commit it alongside `go.mod`.

questions.prompt: Which statements about the Go toolchain are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: `go vet` reports likely bugs the compiler still accepts
`./...` means the current directory and all packages beneath it
`go mod tidy` syncs go.mod with the code's imports
You must install a separate formatter and test runner

questions.explanation: vet finds suspicious constructs, `./...` targets the whole module, and `go mod tidy` reconciles dependencies. Formatting and testing are built into the one `go` command — no separate tools.

questions.prompt: Match each go command to its job.

pairs.right: Build and install a command onto your PATH

questions.explanation: Each blade of the toolchain has a distinct job; `go get` manages dependencies while `go install` places runnable commands on your PATH.

options.text: The official Go language server that powers editor features
A replacement for the go command

questions.explanation: `gopls` gives editors autocompletion, go-to-definition, inline errors, and format-on-save.
